saints.name: St. Gabriel of Our Lady of Sorrows
saints.title: Religious
saints.shortBlurb: A lighthearted young man of Assisi who left the world for the Passionists and reached great holiness before dying at twenty-three…
biography: Francis Possenti was born at Assisi on 1 March 1838, the eleventh of thirteen children of a government lawyer, and was raised at Spoleto, where his charm and love of dancing and dress made him the darling of society. Twice in grave illness he promised God his life in religion, and twice forgot the vow.

In 1856, during a procession of an ancient image of Our Lady of Sorrows in Spoleto's cathedral, he felt an inward voice ask why he lingered in the world. That September he entered the Passionist novitiate at Morrovalle, taking the name Gabriel of Our Lady of Sorrows.

His religious life was outwardly uneventful: exact observance of the rule, cheerful penance, and tender devotion to the sorrows of Mary. Stricken with tuberculosis, he died on 27 February 1862 at Isola del Gran Sasso in the Abruzzi, a seminarian not yet ordained, aged twenty-three.

Beatified by Pope Pius X in 1908 and canonized by Pope Benedict XV in 1920, he was named patron of Catholic youth and students, having sanctified the years of study; in 1959 Pope John XXIII declared him patron of the Abruzzi region, where he died and lies buried.
saints.knownFor: His hidden holiness and joyful devotion to Our Lady of Sorrows.

sources.text: Catholic Encyclopedia (1913), “Bl. Gabriel of Our Lady of Sorrows”
